title: Speed vs Velocity
shared_aspect: Kinematics: Quantifying the rate of positional motion over time.
key_differences_json: [{"criterion": "Mathematical Nature", "concept_a_val": "Scalar quantity (magnitude only, e.g. 50 m/s)", "concept_b_val": "Vector quantity (magnitude + direction, e.g. 50 m/s North)"}, {"criterion": "Sign & Negative Values", "concept_a_val": "Strictly non-negative (>= 0)", "concept_b_val": "Can be negative depending on coordinate axis definition"}, {"criterion": "Calculation Formula", "concept_a_val": "Total Distance / Elapsed Time", "concept_b_val": "Displacement Vector / Elapsed Time"}, {"criterion": "Circular Motion Example", "concept_a_val": "Car on circular track at 60 km/h has constant speed", "concept_b_val": "Car on circular track has continuously changing velocity due to directional turning"}]
common_confusion: Everyday language uses them interchangeably, causing students to forget that turning at constant speed still involves non-zero acceleration.
rule_of_thumb: If direction matters (or can cancel out over a round trip returning to start), it is Velocity. If only magnitude matters, it is Speed.

title: Mass vs Weight
shared_aspect: Classical Mechanics: Quantities associated with gravitational and inertial properties of matter.
key_differences_json: [{"criterion": "Physical Definition", "concept_a_val": "Intrinsic measure of matter and inertia; resistance to acceleration", "concept_b_val": "Gravitational downward force exerted on that mass (W = m*g)"}, {"criterion": "SI Units", "concept_a_val": "Kilograms (kg)", "concept_b_val": "Newtons (N)"}, {"criterion": "Location Dependency", "concept_a_val": "Invariant across the universe (same on Earth, Moon, or in deep space)", "concept_b_val": "Varies directly with local gravitational acceleration (Moon weight is 1/6th of Earth)"}, {"criterion": "Measurement Tool", "concept_a_val": "Balance scale (comparing unknown mass against reference masses)", "concept_b_val": "Spring scale or strain gauge (measuring gravitational pull)"}]
common_confusion: Scales in everyday commerce display kilograms for weight, confounding the force of gravity with intrinsic mass.
rule_of_thumb: Mass is what you are made of (does not change on the Moon); Weight is how hard gravity pulls on that mass.

title: TCP vs UDP
shared_aspect: Computer Networking: Transport Layer (Layer 4) host-to-host data delivery protocols.
key_differences_json: [{"criterion": "Connection Paradigm", "concept_a_val": "Connection-oriented (3-way handshake SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK before transmission)", "concept_b_val": "Connectionless (fire-and-forget datagrams without pre-handshake)"}, {"criterion": "Reliability & Ordering", "concept_a_val": "Guaranteed delivery, automatic packet retransmission, and in-order sequence assembly", "concept_b_val": "No guarantee of packet delivery, ordering, or deduplication"}, {"criterion": "Overhead & Latency", "concept_a_val": "Higher latency (20-byte header, ACKs, flow control, congestion backoff)", "concept_b_val": "Minimal latency and low overhead (8-byte header, zero ACKs)"}, {"criterion": "Ideal Use Cases", "concept_a_val": "Web browsing (HTTP/HTTPS), file transfer (FTP), email (SMTP), financial transactions", "concept_b_val": "Real-time gaming, live video streaming, DNS lookups, VoIP audio"}]
common_confusion: Assuming TCP is always better because it is 'reliable'—in real-time audio, waiting for retransmitted old packets causes unacceptable stutter.
rule_of_thumb: If every byte must arrive intact without corruption: use TCP. If speed matters more than losing an occasional frame: use UDP.

title: Compiler vs Interpreter
shared_aspect: Computer Science: Translating high-level human-readable code into executable machine instructions.
key_differences_json: [{"criterion": "Translation Timing", "concept_a_val": "Ahead-Of-Time (AOT): Translates entire program once before runtime", "concept_b_val": "Just-In-Time (JIT) or line-by-line: Translates instructions dynamically as code executes"}, {"criterion": "Output Artifact", "concept_a_val": "Standalone native binary executable (.exe, ELF, Mach-O)", "concept_b_val": "No standalone binary; requires interpreter runtime environment to execute source/bytecode"}, {"criterion": "Execution Speed", "concept_a_val": "Very fast execution speed; deep compiler optimization passes (LLVM, GCC)", "concept_b_val": "Slower execution speed due to runtime interpretation overhead"}, {"criterion": "Error Detection", "concept_a_val": "Catches syntax and static type errors completely before any code runs", "concept_b_val": "Syntax or runtime type errors encountered only when execution reaches that line"}]
common_confusion: Classifying programming languages as strictly 'compiled' or 'interpreted'—modern environments (Java JVM, Python PyPy, JavaScript V8) combine bytecode compilation with JIT interpretation.
rule_of_thumb: Compilers translate before you run; Interpreters translate as you run.

title: Correlation vs Causation
shared_aspect: Statistics & Epistemology: Evaluating statistical relationships between observed variables.
key_differences_json: [{"criterion": "Definition", "concept_a_val": "Statistical association where two variables move together predictably (e.g. Pearson r)", "concept_b_val": "Direct causal mechanism where altering variable X directly forces an outcome in variable Y"}, {"criterion": "Confounding Factors", "concept_a_val": "Vulnerable to lurking third variables (e.g. ice cream sales and drowning both rise in summer)", "concept_b_val": "Controls for confounding variables via randomized controlled trials (RCTs)"}, {"criterion": "Directionality", "concept_a_val": "Symmetric: corr(A, B) equals corr(B, A)", "concept_b_val": "Asymmetric: X causes Y does not imply Y causes X"}, {"criterion": "Experimental Proof", "concept_a_val": "Can be demonstrated with observational data alone", "concept_b_val": "Requires experimental intervention, counterfactual analysis, or causal graphs"}]
common_confusion: Assuming that because two trends align graphically or statistically, one must be causing the other.
rule_of_thumb: Correlation shows that two things happened together; Causation proves that one made the other happen.

title: Mitosis vs Meiosis
shared_aspect: Cellular Biology & Genetics: Nuclear division in eukaryotic cells.
key_differences_json: [{"criterion": "Purpose & Function", "concept_a_val": "Growth, tissue repair, and asexual reproduction", "concept_b_val": "Production of gametes (sperm and egg cells) for sexual reproduction"}, {"criterion": "Daughter Cells Produced", "concept_a_val": "2 identical diploid (2n) daughter cells", "concept_b_val": "4 genetically distinct haploid (n) daughter cells"}, {"criterion": "Rounds of Division", "concept_a_val": "1 division cycle (Prophase, Metaphase, Anaphase, Telophase)", "concept_b_val": "2 sequential division cycles (Meiosis I and Meiosis II)"}, {"criterion": "Genetic Recombination", "concept_a_val": "No crossing over; produces exact genetic clones", "concept_b_val": "Homologous crossing over and independent assortment generate high diversity"}]
common_confusion: Mixing up chromosome count outcomes, forgetting that meiosis halves the genetic complement so fertilization restores the diploid count.
rule_of_thumb: Mitosis makes identical copies for MY body (somatic); Meiosis makes unique cells for reproduction.

title: Hypothesis vs Scientific Theory
shared_aspect: Philosophy of Science: Explanatory scientific propositions.
key_differences_json: [{"criterion": "Scope & Maturity", "concept_a_val": "A tentative, testable proposed explanation for an empirical observation", "concept_b_val": "A comprehensive, extensively tested, and corroborated framework explaining nature"}, {"criterion": "Evidentiary Backing", "concept_a_val": "May have minimal initial empirical data; awaiting testing", "concept_b_val": "Supported by vast bodies of independent empirical evidence across decades"}, {"criterion": "Colloquial Confusion", "concept_a_val": "Matches the everyday word 'guess'", "concept_b_val": "NOT a guess; represents the highest tier of scientific certainty (e.g. Germ Theory, Plate Tectonics)"}, {"criterion": "Falsifiability", "concept_a_val": "Must propose concrete predictions that could be proven false", "concept_b_val": "Continuously refined as new precise instruments challenge edge cases"}]
common_confusion: Saying 'it is only a theory' dismisses a well-tested scientific framework by confusing it with an unsubstantiated hypothesis.
rule_of_thumb: A hypothesis is a question waiting to be tested; a theory is an overarching explanation backed by mountains of evidence.

title: RAM vs Secondary Storage
shared_aspect: Computer Architecture: Digital hardware for storing binary program data and instructions.
key_differences_json: [{"criterion": "Volatility", "concept_a_val": "Volatile: contents vanish instantly when electric power is lost", "concept_b_val": "Non-volatile: data persists indefinitely without electric power (NAND Flash / HDD)"}, {"criterion": "Access Latency", "concept_a_val": "Ultra-fast direct CPU access: ~10 to 80 nanoseconds", "concept_b_val": "Slower block I/O access: ~10 to 100 microseconds (NVMe SSD) or milliseconds (HDD)"}, {"criterion": "System Role", "concept_a_val": "Workspace holding actively executing OS code, open applications, and live runtime memory", "concept_b_val": "Archive holding installed software, user files, media, and dormant data"}, {"criterion": "Cost per Gigabyte", "concept_a_val": "Significantly higher cost per gigabyte", "concept_b_val": "Low cost per gigabyte; orders of magnitude larger capacities"}]
common_confusion: Users saying their computer has '512 GB of memory' when they mean 512 GB of SSD storage and only 16 GB of RAM.
rule_of_thumb: RAM is your desk where you work right now; Storage is the filing cabinet where you keep files when you are done.
